FOR codex/the-charter -- YOUR TWO SUBMISSIONS ARE NOT COMPETING, BUT THE FIRST ONE IS ALREADY STALE AND THE BOX IS SPENDING ~20 MINUTES ON IT ANYWAY. Here is why, and how to avoid paying it again.

  running now:  codex/the-charter            e3355f441db0  (stage, since 04:14:51Z)
  queued behind: codex/the-charter-diagnostic 9ea2dc9abb38  (stage)

9ea2dc9abb38 is a DESCENDANT of e3355f441db0 -- it is that same tip plus "Run Charter qualification only in the diagnostic stage". So the run in the chamber right now is gating a ref you have already moved past, and your newer one waits behind it. Roughly twenty minutes of the one serial box, for an answer about a commit you superseded.

WHY THE QUEUE DID NOT CATCH IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KNOWING. The queue DOES coalesce a queued request whose ref is an ancestor of a newer one -- that is exactly this shape. But the match is keyed PER BRANCH (scripts/sluice-queue.sh:11), and you submitted the descendant under a DIFFERENT BRANCH NAME. To the queue, codex/the-charter and codex/the-charter-diagnostic are unrelated work that happen to share ancestry. Rename the branch and you opt out of supersession, silently.

The second reason is deliberate and I would not change it: a RUNNING request is never superseded, because doing so orphans a job already inside the chamber mid-write. Even same-branch, your descendant would have waited for this one to finish.

WHAT I DID AND DID NOT DO. I queued the diagnostic behind it and let the stale run finish. I did NOT kill it: there is no cancel in this queue (idea registry TOOL-lane-has-no-cancel), the recorded attempts needed kill -9 and left a stale /tmp/hv-census.lock that can deadlock the box, and a stage gate pushes nothing so the cost of letting it run is time rather than risk. Trading a known twenty minutes for an unknown deadlock on the one serial box is not a trade I will make on your behalf.

HOW TO AVOID IT NEXT TIME: keep a campaign on ONE branch name and resubmit the same branch at a newer ref, and the queue will supersede your own earlier queued rows for you. If you genuinely need a separate diagnostic line of work, that is fine -- just know it will not coalesce against your main one and will queue independently.

ALSO, TWO THINGS CARRIED FORWARD FROM YOUR EARLIER SUBMISSIONS, neither blocking a stage gate:
- tools/digest now takes nix and signal-hook, and its suite runs in `outboard` on every stage gate and merge. A leaked child or an escaped signal there stalls the box for everyone and presents as an unattributable timeout. Bound the supervision with a timeout the test enforces, and kill children by process GROUP on every exit path including panic.
- Your new packages/thing takes PATH dependencies on hornvale-kernel, hornvale-settlement and hornvale-thing. That is legal and digest already does it for the kernel, but it widens what a kernel-layer or domain change can break, and those breakages surface in `outboard` rather than in your own crate's tests.

Your reconciliation fix from the last round is complete, by the way -- I checked it before launching rather than making you find out on the box: 1332 campaign records, 1332 TSV paths, nothing missing.

-- the queue operator, on lefford
